chose: put enrich/backfill SQL (write transaction, claim query) in lib/load.ts instead of steps.ts
over: keeping persistence logic in steps.ts next to the classify.ts import
because: steps.ts must statically import classify.ts, which classify.ts's own author was still writing in parallel; keeping lib/load.ts classify-free let its own *.db.test.ts run and pass against the real database before classify.ts existed, and the allowed-files list only permitted lib/db.ts + lib/load.ts as new lib files

chose: backfill force=true widens the claim query to the whole corpus (ignoring status/classifier_version), and is forwarded to each enrich child's payload
over: treating force as a no-op on the claim SQL since the plan's §7.2 prose only lists the missing/stale/behind-version predicate
because: BackfillPayload.force is documented as 're-classify even when the fingerprint and classifier version already match' — that only has an observable effect if the claim itself can select rows the default staleness predicate would exclude; otherwise force would never do anything a plain backfill run does not already do

chose: backfill claim SQL is a UNION ALL of two CTE arms (missing recipe_enrichment row via anti-join on recipe; stale/behind-version row driven from recipe_enrichment)
over: one recipe LEFT JOIN recipe_enrichment WHERE clause
because: the plan names recipe_enrichment (status, classifier_version) as the index the claim must actually use; a single LEFT JOIN driven from recipe would probe that index once per recipe row (nested loop) rather than letting Postgres scan it directly for the out-of-date rows, and the missing-row case can never be found through that index anyway since it requires an anti-join

chose: enrich step catches writeEnrichment's error, records status='error' via markError, then re-throws
over: swallowing the error after recording it (returning a normal {status:'error'} result instead)
because: the step declares attempts:3 with exponential backoff; swallowing the error would make the job complete on the first try and BullMQ would never retry it, defeating the retry policy the plan explicitly specifies — matches the idiom atproto-sync's sync-repo already uses (markRepoError then throw)

chose: no new invariant for patch c4c9d65a5447dc5e
over: add an invariant or boundary claim that the change does not require
because: recipe-enrichment workflow (§7): the correctness-critical behaviors are already pinned as executable assertions in lib/load.db.test.ts (cascade delete produces no 23001, writeEnrichment replaces labels wholesale rather than merging, claimBatch's ordering/remaining/force/localOnly), and steps.ts/index.ts are thin orchestration over that tested layer with no independent invariant of their own to anchor
